scopeNote.value: General-purpose construction/generation link — e.g. the CyberActivity realizing a Step is what actually constructs the value a Variable ends up stonework:boundTo, or a complex output artifact (a dataset, a report) that value refers to.

definition.value: Temporal succession of Information (v1 precedes v2 of a report)
Shortcut triple: generic relationship. Corresponds to STIX relationship_type 'related-to'.
Relates infrastructure to the Agent recorded as its owner or registrant of record — the entity in whose name the resource is officially registered.
A globally unique identifier for a BOM document, typically expressed as a URN UUID (e.g. urn:uuid:...) per the CycloneDX specification or as a document namespace per SPDX.

scopeNote.value: Domain intentionally left unset. Primary subject is stonework:SoftwareBillOfMaterials. Use dcterms:created for the BOM timestamp.

definition.value: Shortcut triple: source STIX object is revoked and superseded by target. Corresponds to STIX relationship_type 'revoked-by'.
The literal value that guardVariable's bound value is compared against.

scopeNote.value: Compared using the operator given by stonework:guardOperator; if guardOperator is omitted, comparison defaults to Equals. Must share a compatible, numerically-typed datatype with the guardVariable's stonework:boundToLiteral value when an ordering operator is used.

definition.value: Relates a product family to a specific versioned product instance.
The Step a Transition leaves.
Links any individual to one or more contextual categories.

scopeNote.value: This is the primary mechanism for flexible, context-sensitive classification (e.g., Evidence, HighValue, Suspect, etc.). Multiple categories per individual are allowed.

definition.value: Links a Technique to the Tactic(s) it achieves or supports.

scopeNote.value: This is the inverse of hasTechnique. A single Technique may support multiple Tactics (e.g. 'Phishing' supports both Initial Access and Credential Access).

definition.value: Relates an Agent to a product family it develops or maintains.
Relates a source DetectionRule, Sensor, Indicator, or defensive technique to the threat, activity, or artifact it is capable of detecting. Corresponds to STIX relationship_type 'detects'.

scopeNote.value: Domain/range intentionally left unset: this property is a direct lift of the STIX 2.1 relationship_type 'detects' shortcut. STIX does not schema-constrain which SDO/SCO types may appear as source_ref/target_ref for a given relationship_type — that's producer convention, not enforceable structure, and a closed domain/range here would misrepresent real STIX 2.1 data and mislead reasoner-based consumers.

definition.value: Links a CyberActivity to the CyberEntity it acted upon — the asset, artifact, or resource the activity operated against.

scopeNote.value: Mirrors prov:used (an Activity used an Entity). Typical range instances are stonework:Host, stonework:RuntimeProcess, or other stonework:DigitalArtifact/stonework:Infrastructure individuals — e.g. the specific lsass.exe stonework:RuntimeProcess a credential-dumping attempt acted on. Distinct from stonework:targets: targets is a direct, open-domain/range lift of the STIX 2.1 relationship_type 'targets' shortcut, describing higher-level strategic targeting (a Sector, a Location, an Agent) by a Campaign/MalwareSample/ThreatActor. actsOn is purpose-built for the concrete technical asset one execution-trace Activity acted upon — the same distinction develop draws between stonework:mitigates (open, STIX-lifted) and stonework:mitigatesAttackPattern (purpose-built, controlled domain/range).

definition.value: Relates an entity to an AttackPattern representing the same underlying technique in a different framework shape, resolved from a shared technique identifier (e.g. a CAPEC entry and the MITRE ATT&CK technique it maps to, or a CWE weakness and the CAPEC pattern that exploits it).

scopeNote.value: Domain intentionally left unset: subjects include stonework:Weakness (CWE → CAPEC) and stonework:AttackPattern itself (CAPEC → ATT&CK). Materialized by joining a framework's technique-identifier literal (see stonework:relatedTechniqueIdentifier) against the ATT&CK technique's external reference. Framework ontologies declare their concrete property (e.g. capec:relatedAttackTechnique, cwe:relatedAttackPattern) as rdfs:subPropertyOf this.

definition.value: The CVSS vector string encoding the metric values used to compute the headline base score, e.g. 'CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H'.
An optional ordinal position for a Step within a strictly linear Behavior, where the full precededByStep graph is unnecessary.

scopeNote.value: Most CTI procedure write-ups (a numbered list of adversary actions) are linear. stepOrder is a low-overhead alternative to precededByStep for that common case; the two are not mutually exclusive.

definition.value: Relates a weakness to the vulnerability that exploits or instantiates it.

scopeNote.value: The range is a vulnerability individual. The weakness individual (domain) is a stonework:Weakness whose IRI is derived from the CWE identifier. The weakness individual may be populated by a separate CWE ingest.
